global.title: Web project conventions
global.tagline: Give your agent the habits of a careful senior web developer, from the first commit.
global.summary: Starting instructions for any website or web app: semantic HTML, WCAG 2.1 AA, design tokens, fluid CSS, SOLID structure, forms, loading states and secure server defaults.
highlights: Semantic HTML and WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility on every component
Colours, font sizes and spacing as :root tokens with fluid clamp() scaling
Two modal types, dismissible or not, with shared global styling
Forms with inline, as-you-type guidance and password rules that accept browser-suggested passwords
Skeletons, empty and error states for every async operation
Server-side validation, authorization and correct HTTP status codes, with no leaked internals
Branded 404, safe redirects and unique page titles
usageSteps: Save it in your project's root, then add the line `@global.md` to your `CLAUDE.md` so Claude Code loads it in every session. With no `CLAUDE.md` yet, rename the file to `CLAUDE.md` instead.
Work as usual. The agent applies the conventions to every file it creates or changes, and follows your codebase where it already does things differently.
Add a framework-specific file, such as `nextjs-structure.md`, on top of it for project structure.

nextjs-structure.title: Next.js project structure
nextjs-structure.tagline: Stop asking where the file goes. Your agent already knows.
nextjs-structure.summary: Where every file goes in a Next.js App Router project: src/ layout, routes-only app/, component folders, server-only code, public/ assets, aliases, titles and route protection.
highlights: A complete src/ tree showing where every kind of file belongs
app/ holds routes only, with the home page in a (homepage) route group
Component folders per route, per feature and global/, with no loose files
Server-only code in src/server/, guarded with server-only imports
Static files in public/; paid or private files served through an access-checked route
@/* imports with no barrel files, and one title template for every page
proxy.ts for redirects, with real permission checks in every handler
usageSteps: Save it in your project's root, then add the line `@nextjs-structure.md` to your `CLAUDE.md` so Claude Code loads it in every session.
On a new project, ask the agent to scaffold it following the file. On an existing one, it keeps your current structure where it differs and tells you about the difference.
Let the agent keep the structure section of your `CLAUDE.md` current as it adds routes and folders.

dev-tools-advisor.title: Dev tools and stack advisor
dev-tools-advisor.tagline: Let your agent research the tools that fit your project, not the ones in fashion.
dev-tools-advisor.summary: Recommends a linter, formatter, test runner, package manager, framework or library from your project and your setup: it detects your environment, researches current docs and respects the tools you already chose.
highlights: Detects your OS, editor, version manager and stack before recommending anything
Asks only what it can't read from the repo, and offers to save your setup so other projects don't ask again
Researches each tool's current docs and maintenance instead of recommending from memory
Compares by compatibility, simplicity, editor integration and migration cost
One recommendation and one alternative, with exact commands for your shell and package manager
Respects your decisions: if you already chose a tool, it sets it up well instead of arguing
Records every decision in the project's instructions so it isn't reopened
usageSteps: Save it in your project's root and reference it from the instruction file your agent reads (for example the line `@dev-tools-advisor.md` in `CLAUDE.md`, or its content in `AGENTS.md` or your Cursor rules).

Run it right away by sending your agent a prompt. In a project in progress: `Follow dev-tools-advisor.md and review the tools in this project.` In an empty folder: `Follow dev-tools-advisor.md and recommend a stack for a booking web app.` The agent detects your setup and asks only for what's missing.
From then on, ask about a single tool whenever you need it (for example "ESLint and Prettier, or Biome?"), or start a new project, and the agent applies the advisor on its own.
Approve the recommendation. The agent installs it, runs it once to confirm it works, and records the decision.
